On September 9, 2026, Hudson Pacific Properties and its joint venture partner executed an Extension and Loan Modification Agreement on the $1.1 billion CMBS mortgage secured by their Hollywood Media Portfolio, with the press release issued September 11, 2026. The transaction extended the loan’s maturity to November 9, 2027, kept the stated interest rate unchanged and required no principal repayment, easing near-term refinancing risk and preserving liquidity for the office REIT.

The 2.2 million-square-foot Hollywood Media Portfolio comprises three major studio lots—Sunset Gower, Sunset Las Palmas and Sunset Bronson—plus five Class A office properties and rights to build an additional 1.1 million square feet of office and production space, of which Hudson Pacific owns 51 percent and manages leasing and operations. As part of the extension, the joint venture reallocated funds to create a $20 million leasing and capital reserve, with excess cash flow swept into this reserve, and Hudson Pacific entered a SOFR swap at 3.50 percent to manage interest expense, collectively supporting its leasing strategy and long-term capital planning for these flagship media assets.

data.title: Lixiang Education Narrows First-Half 2026 Loss But Flags Going-Concern Risks
data.description:
Lixiang Education Holding Co ( (LXEH) ) has issued an announcement.

Net revenues for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were RMB15.2 million, little changed from a year earlier, as declines in tuition and accommodation income were balanced by stronger sales from in-house canteen operations, healthcare support services and other ancillary activities. Lixiang Education reported a turnaround to RMB2.7 million in gross profit from a RMB5.0 million gross loss in 2025, reflecting deep cuts in rental, labour, healthcare service and tax-related costs.

Operating expenses climbed to RMB13.0 million, mainly due to higher professional service fees, but the company’s net loss narrowed to RMB11.4 million and net loss per ADS improved after an April 20, 2026 reverse stock split and ADS ratio change. Despite this operational improvement, cash fell to RMB9.4 million and large accumulated and working capital deficits continue to cast doubt on its ability to remain a going concern, while a favorable 2025 arbitration award for over RMB90 million has produced only minimal recovery so far, leaving a key potential source of funds uncertain for investors and creditors.

More about Lixiang Education Holding Co

Lixiang Education Holding Co., Ltd., listed on NASDAQ as LXEH, is a private education service provider based in Lishui, Zhejiang, China. Its revenues come from tuition and accommodation at its schools, sales of meals, uniforms and learning materials, healthcare support services, and related offerings such as course design, training, flexible employment services and rental income.

The company also operates Langfang School, where it has shifted canteen operations in-house, and healthcare service businesses driven by Hebei Chuangxiang. These diversified activities reflect a broader strategy to supplement traditional private schooling income with ancillary services, amid an increasingly competitive student recruitment environment in China’s education market.

Net revenues for the six months ended June 30, 2026 were RMB15.2 million, broadly flat year-on-year, as lower tuition and accommodation income was offset by growth in canteen and healthcare support services. Despite the modest revenue change, Lixiang Education turned a gross profit of RMB2.7 million from a gross loss of RMB5.0 million a year earlier, largely due to significant cost reductions at Langfang School and efficiency gains in its healthcare operations.

Cost of revenues fell sharply to RMB12.6 million from RMB20.4 million, driven by lower rental, labour, healthcare service costs and taxes, though total operating expenses rose to RMB13.0 million on higher professional service fees. The company’s net loss narrowed to RMB11.4 million from RMB16.1 million, and net loss per ADS improved following an April 20, 2026 1-for-10 reverse stock split and ADS ratio change, yet cash declined to RMB9.4 million and substantial accumulated and working capital deficits continue to raise going concern risks.

Management warns that existing working capital is insufficient to fund operations for the next 12 months without new financing, and is exploring debt extensions, equity or strategic investment options and stricter cost controls, with no assurance of success. A separate arbitration case saw subsidiary Lishui Mengxiang win a RMB72.41 million contract claim and RMB20 million liquidated damages in April 2025, but enforcement has so far yielded only RMB327.9, leaving the award largely unrealized and underscoring ongoing uncertainty for stakeholders.
